content.rendered:
Based on the film that starred Jack Lemmon, Tony Curtis, and Marilyn Monroe, this Broadway hit gives a classic story new life with music and lyrics from the creators of Hairspray, Marc Shaiman and Scott Wittman. The super-smart book and lyrics by Tony Award-winning playwright Matthew Lopez (Inheritance) and Late Night star Amber Ruffin update the vibe to suit 21st-century audiences, telling the hilarious story of two 1930s jazz musicians who go on the run from the mob disguised as women as part of an all-female band headed to California. Just like in the movie, Joe and Jerry become Josephine and Daphne, become “friendly” with the band’s star singer Sugar Kane, and find themselves transformed by the experience – and in ways a 1950s film could never make explicit. This tap-heavy, dance-intensive, Prohibition-era spectacle retains a comic heart of pure gold as co-author Lopez reminds us, “we don’t think men in dresses are funny, but we think idiots in trouble are always funny.”  Get your tickets now, especially if you want to be one of the lucky patrons every night to sit at the cabaret tables surrounding the stage!

Welcome to Leech Woods

According to Montgomery County historical land records, the present site of Leech Woods was originally settled by Warwick and Jeanne Leech and their six children sometime in early 1790.  Having immigrated from Hungary, the family chose Damascus, Maryland, based on its temperate climate and heavily wooded region, which reminded them of their homeland.  The Leech family store thrived as the leading local merchant of hides, furs, and hunting supplies.  During the disastrous Winter of 1804, the Leech family store was robbed and vandalized by unknown attackers and the body of John Leech, the youngest son, was found nailed to the back wall of the store.  The remaining bodies of the family members were later found bludgeoned and bound inside of the root cellar of their homestead.  No further information about the attackers or motives for the killings is known.

​Remnants of the Leech family homestead still stand deep in the woods where the present Leech Woods experience is built.  The Leech Woods immersive experience follows the original walking path from the site of the Leech family hunting supply store to the remnants of the original family homestead.  As the property was classified as a historical site in 1972, no artifacts may be removed, and we ask that you respect the privacy of the grave sites. 

What’s new?

More Scares. More scenes. More Screams. We added 6 new scenes to the original trail to bring you even more terror. The Horror Hayride also has new scenes added to the 20-minute ride/walk-through.

What to expect

Leech Woods is a thirty-minute immersive haunted trail experience of dark terror. We promise a night of chainsaws, clowns, and dark corners. When you are done screaming, we offer amazing food and drinks, alcoholic beverages, bonfires, glow-in-the-dark axe-throwing, fire dancers, a DJ booth, fortune telling, and other forms of entertainment every night in the Leech Woods Midway, where Admission Is Free. 

Trail

What is our Trail?

Leech Woods is one of the scariest haunted trails in all of Maryland. It’s about a 30-minute walk with now over 15 highly detailed immersive walkthrough scenes, all enhanced this year with even more scares. Plus, our trail has over 50 professionally trained scarers. You can check out our gallery to see photos of our trail and actors.

Recommend age: 12+

HORROR HAYRIDE

What is the Horror Hayride?

The Horror Hayride is a 20-minute ride and walk-through full of brand new, highly detailed, immersive scenes. On this trail, you discover what is believed to be the Leech Woods family cemetery. Limited to 25 victims per trip. Please respect the graves and reserve your seats now. ​

Recommended Age: 12+

title.rendered: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre

content.rendered:
Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget.

By Washington Irving
Adapted by Nathan Weinberger
Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili
Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili

Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

Although he’s keeping the details under wraps, Brown has said that with An Evening of Alton Brown, he’s “stirring up some twists on his greatest hits,” and “spicing things up with new demonstrations, music, and slightly scaled-down mayhem.”  No matter what, An Evening of Alton Brown will present Brown as you’ve never seen him — unless, of course, you’ve been invited to his house.

Best known for creating and hosting groundbreaking television such as Good Eats, Iron Chef America, Cutthroat Kitchen, and Food Network Star, Brown has also built one of the most successful culinary touring franchises ever, performing live in more than 300 cities for well over half a million fans. With An Evening of Alton Brown, he strips away the spectacle in favor of connection, spontaneity, and storytelling, delivering a show that is equal part humor, science, food, and heart.

Lori Rounds and “Reimagined”
Mini-Solo for Richard Svec

(Rockville, MD) – Artists & Makers Studios is pleased to host Lori Rounds for the month of October. The exhibit will run from September 30th through October 28th, with a First Friday opening on October 2nd from 5-8pm. Reimagined marks a period of transition in Lori Niland Rounds’ artistic practice – one shaped by interruption, adaptation, and a changing way of seeing.

Faced with an unexpected challenge that made familiar methods of working more difficult, Rounds began to reconsider both process and possibility. What initially felt like constraint gradually opened a different path forward, inviting experimentation with new gestures, materials, and ways of making. Richard Svec shares a mini-solo exhibit in the Lounge Gallery and Resident Artists exhibit new work in the Gallery Hall. Enjoy the sculptural work of Francis Maduka Uduh in studio 11, along with nineteen Gallery 209 Member Artists exhibiting their latest work. content.rendered:
How can diverse experiences strengthen leadership, expand economic opportunity, and help shape Montgomery County’s future?

Join Maryland State Delegate and USG Board of Advisors member Lily Qi for a candid conversation inspired by her memoir, Elected American: From Red China to Blue Maryland. Together with USG Executive Director Dr. Anne Khademian and Montgomery County Chamber of Commerce President and CEO Angela Franco, Lily will explore her journey from immigrant newcomer to elected leader—and share insights on inclusive leadership, civic participation, the regional economy, and building a more connected and competitive community.

Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget.

By Washington Irving
Adapted by Nathan Weinberger
Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili
Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili

With a fresh set of questions each week, every round is a chance to prove you’re the sharpest in the room. Whether you’re a trivia pro or just in it for the fun, all are welcome.

Join us every Wednesday from 7–9 PM and make it a midweek tradition.

title.rendered: K/NOW Dialogue with Joan Danziger and Floyd Shockley “Beetlemania!”

content.rendered: Join American sculptor and Washington gem Joan Danziger, along with Smithsonian Museum of Natural History chief entomologist Floyd Shockley, as we examine human history’s fascination, indeed its reliance, on the beetle. Danziger’s sculptures radiate the strength and beauty of these creatures in her ongoing exhibition “Beetlemania!” Dr. Shockley’s deep knowledge of the vastness of beetle life will help us understand this wonder of Mother Earth.

title.rendered: Sugar Skulls for Dia de los Muertos

content.rendered: Celebrate tradition through art! In this all-ages workshop, you’ll be supplied with everything you need to decorate your very own ceramic sugar skull to take home and display. Spend an evening painting your skull and adorning it with marigolds, all while learning about the rich history, traditions, and cultural impact of Dia de los Muertos.

Afro-Cuban All Stars is a multigenerational orchestra devoted to promoting the full range of Cuban music, bringing together musicians across styles and eras. Led by bandleader Juan de Marcos González—also a central figure in the Buena Vista Social Club project—the ensemble reflects a long-standing approach rooted in tradition while embracing contemporary Cuban sounds. Their program moves across son, bolero, and rhythm-driven dance styles, drawing on the musical traditions of Cuba’s mid-20th-century golden age.

Founded in the 1990s, the group continues to evolve through a flexible lineup that incorporates younger musicians alongside established artists. More than a fixed ensemble, Afro-Cuban All Stars operates as a shifting orchestra, adapting its sound to reflect different periods and styles, grounded in González’s concept of building on musical roots while creating space for the future.

title.rendered: Flying Buddha presents Bad Behavior: Villains

content.rendered:
Heroes follow the rules. Villains write them.

Bad Behavior returns with its darkest production yet. Villains is a theatrical pole cabaret celebrating the unforgettable characters audiences secretly love most.

Across six captivating acts, you’ll encounter criminal masterminds, queens of darkness, seductive manipulators, monsters, and agents of chaos brought to life through pole dance, movement, music, and immersive storytelling.

Set inside the intimate Side Bar at ON St. Elmo, this 90-minute experience combines cinematic performances with handcrafted cocktails and an energetic nightlife atmosphere.

Whether you’re drawn to comic book legends, gothic queens, classic movie villains, or the beautifully misunderstood antihero, Villains invites you to embrace your dark side for one unforgettable night.

Ticket cost: $40

Important Information: Doors open at 6:30pm — guests are encouraged to arrive early to enjoy ON St. Elmo’s craft cocktails and seasonal American Coastal Mediterranean-inspired cuisine before the show begins promptly at 8:30pm. There is a $25 food and beverage minimum. Cocktails and bites are available à la carte. Tickets include the show only. Tipping performers is encouraged and always appreciated.

title.rendered: OLD LINE MARKET: Vintage, Garden & Artisan Market

content.rendered: Come spend the day with us shopping high quality vintage, garden and artisan vendors.  Old Line Market is held at the historic Aix La Chapelle Farm in Poolesville, Maryland on Friday from 10-5, Saturday from 10-5 and Sunday from 10-4.  Enjoy your weekend shopping in a village-like setting in and amongst beautifully restored historic barns, grounds, and tents. Food trucks, local wine and craft beer available. Plenty of free parking, and admission is good for both days, those under 18 are free.  Dog and kid friendly.

title.rendered: Gallery B Presents “Layered Lives: Women in Print:

content.rendered:
October 9, 2026 – November 1, 2026
Gallery Hours: Friday-Saturday, 12-5pm; Sunday, 11am-2pm
Opening Reception: Friday, October 9, 6-8pm

Layered Lives: Women in Print brings together women artists from the DMV region who explore the depths of lived experience through experimental printmaking techniques. Working primarily in semi-abstract forms, the artists use layered images, symbols, and textures—both physical and symbolic to reflect narratives of resilience, identity, and transformation. Through innovative approaches to printmaking, their artworks reveal the enduring power of craft and creative strength, that evolves over time, celebrating the intersection of personal intuition, artistic craft, and collective memory.
